definitions.title: Trigonometric Substitution Dictionary
definitions.latex: \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Radical Form} & \text{Substitution} & \text{Identity} \\ \hline \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} & x = a\sin(\theta) & a^2 - a^2\sin^2(\theta) = a^2\cos^2(\theta) \\ \sqrt{a^2 + x^2} & x = a\tan(\theta) & a^2 + a^2\tan^2(\theta) = a^2\sec^2(\theta) \\ \sqrt{x^2 - a^2} & x = a\sec(\theta) & a^2\sec^2(\theta) - a^2 = a^2\tan^2(\theta) \end{array}
definitions.statement: Trigonometric substitutions eliminate square roots containing quadratic binomials by transforming them into single trigonometric squared terms via Pythagorean identities.
definitions.explanation: Right triangle geometry facilitates back-substitution from theta to original variable x.
definitions.keyTakeaway: sqrt(a^2 - x^2) -> x = a sin theta; sqrt(a^2 + x^2) -> x = a tan theta; sqrt(x^2 - a^2) -> x = a sec theta.
